newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols off highs after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols off highs after Greenspan.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed-income options ended off highs as underlying markets rallied after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the Senate Budget Committee, dealers said.

Implied volatility for March Treasury bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade stood at around 9.6 percent shortly before the close, unchanged from Friday but more than a quarter point off early highs.
"Volatility has kind of yo-yoed today," a CBOT T-bond trader for a brokerage firm. "It was up early...but it's since come off to more unchanged-type levels."
March T-bond futures, which had tumbled to as low as 110-6/32 early in the session, rallied to a high of 111-20/32 after Greenspan's comments.

The Fed chairman did express concerns about inflationary pressures from wages and described the stock market's gains as "breathtaking," but traders said the market had already declined earlier in anticipation of much stronger words.

The brokerage trader said the gamma value of the March contract, which expires on February 21, had become so high that it was difficult to sustain volatility gains for a long time without a big move in bond prices to justify them.
High-gamma options are sensitive to market swings but are vulnerable to time decay.
February options, which have even higher gamma than March as they expire at the end of the week, saw a good amount of speculative put buying early in the day.
"Feb 10 (February 110) puts were the options of choice this morning prior to Greenspan," the brokerage trader said.
Traders said several put and put-spread purchases were also seen early on in 2,000- to 3,000-lot sizes.
At the shorter end of the curve, Eurodollar volatilities were also off early highs but still up from Friday's levels.
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange stood at around 12.5 and 15.5 percent, respectively.
"They did come off, but they were really well bid at the open," a bank affiliate trader said. "We settled on the bid side Friday and there was a lot of buying interest this morning."
He added that few huge deals took place but there was a lot of moderate-sized buying across the board.
Trading in CBOT and CME fixed-income derivatives was closed on Monday due to the Martin Luther King Jr holiday.
